The decay rate difference between $B^0_s$ and its antiparticle is determined by analyzing $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ events, with an emphasis on resolving the distinct mass peaks associated with the short- and long-lived components of the $B^0_s$ system. By incorporating a novel technique that accounts for the impact of background events, an updated assessment of this decay rate difference is achieved, resulting in a value of $0.098\pm 0.011(\textrm{stat})\pm 0.010(\textrm{syst})$.

This paper investigates the semi-discrete approximation of a distributed control problem, where a stochastic equation with a random dispersion term is discretized in space. The domain is divided into smaller sections using a finite element method, and we establish strong convergence of the optimal discretized controls and corresponding states to their continuous counterparts.

Our study investigates high-energy cosmic-ray fluctuations using a comprehensive analysis of 1000 events with energies exceeding 4 EeV, as detected by the Pierre Auger Observatory. By examining the spatial distribution of these high-energy cosmic rays, we found that the measured variance in small-scale fluctuations is in line with the predictions of isotropic diffusion models, which suggest that the most energetic cosmic rays are influenced by magnetic fields on intergalactic scales. Furthermore, we found that the measured large-scale fluctuations are consistent with the predictions of isotropic diffusion models, which suggest that the most energetic cosmic rays are influenced by magnetic fields on intergalactic scales.

This study examines the characteristics of charged particles produced in proton-lead collisions using the ATLAS detector at the CERN Large Hadron Collider. By analyzing data from 2013, we compare the results to those from proton-proton collisions and determine the nuclear alteration factor. The study covers a wide range of transverse momenta and rapidities, and the results are compared to theoretical models. The analysis is performed for both forward and central rapidity regions, and the results are found to be in good agreement with the models.

This study examines the noncommutative quantum mechanical framework, where the spatial coordinates obey a specific algebraic structure defined by the universal enveloping algebra of a given Lie algebra. The analysis focuses on the algebraic properties of the system's Hamiltonian, particularly its ability to be expressed as a polynomial within the same algebraic structure. The study also explores the associated spectral problem and the development of noncommutative harmonic oscillators for specific Lie algebras. The analysis highlights the potential for noncommutative quantum mechanics to provide a unified approach to understanding harmonic oscillators across various algebraic structures. The study further discusses the implications of noncommutative quantum mechanics on the algebraic properties of angular momentum and its applications to angular harmonic problems. In cancer immunotherapy, the response to treatment is influenced by the presence of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, which can be classified into five categories based on their proximity. This study presents a federated learning approach to assist pathologists in determining the category of tumors by analyzing images of tissue cores. The proposed method involves multiple institutions training separate models on their own data and sharing only the model updates to create a unified, accurate system. Our federated learning approach was compared to training a single model on a combined dataset, and the results showed that our method achieved a high level of accuracy, with an F1-score of 0.81, while also preserving data privacy.

In optical communication systems, nonlinear effects can cause short bursts of errors that may spread through a decision feedback equalizer, degrading its performance. To mitigate this issue, we propose using a modified DFE structure that incorporates a burst-error filter, which can be optimized to minimize the spread of errors. Our approach was tested in a real-world scenario involving a 100-km submarine link, where we found that the optimal filter design can significantly reduce error propagation and improve the overall system's bit error rate performance.

Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success in various fields, particularly in time-series analysis. A standout neural network architecture, Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs), has gained significant popularity due to its impressive performance and ease of use. TCNs have demonstrated outstanding results in numerous applications, including speech recognition, music transcription, and fault diagnosis. However, the large size of TCNs poses a challenge for deployment on resource-constrained devices, as it consumes excessive memory and processing power. To address this challenge, we propose a novel and efficient TCN optimization framework called Trimming In Time (PIT). This innovative optimizer leverages a novel pruning technique and a lightweight network structure to reduce the size of TCNs while maintaining their high performance. Our experiments show that PIT can effectively compress TCNs by up to 90% in size, resulting in significant improvements in memory usage, processing speed, and energy consumption. Our framework is particularly effective in a wide range of applications, including speech recognition, music transcription, and fault diagnosis. Overall, our work provides a powerful and versatile tool for deploying TCNs on resource-constrained devices, enabling them to deliver high-quality results in a wide range of time-series analysis applications.

We demonstrate that the multilinear Zinbiel algebras associated with any finite set form an isomorphism class to direct sums of the trivial representation of the symmetric group. Consequently, all Zinbiel algebras derived from any finite-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic zero are isomorphic to direct sums of its direct summands.

By analyzing the angles at which these particles move in the x-y plane, we have determined the distribution of stream angles and found that they fluctuate significantly, with a fluctuation that is independent of transverse momentum. This paper formulates a general method to derive the bijective mapping between a specific logic system and its enhanced variant, known as the lexicographic path ordering with equality. We achieve this by first establishing a simplified form for terms within the original logic system, then demonstrating that terms in the enhanced variant can be uniquely matched to terms in the simplified format. As a practical application, our method is used to develop the reverse correspondence for the extended logic system, NLE-Logics, comprising non-linear term orderings and equality.

We examine the issue of inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values, specifically focusing on dependencies that can be functionally determined.
A relationship is considered determinable if a specific attribute's value can be predicted based on another attribute's value.
Our research aims to identify which functional determinations can be reliably inferred from a given table, even when some values are missing.
We also explore how these inferable determinations can be represented using a new concept called a bifid dependency, which captures the relationship between two attributes that are functionally determined by a third attribute.
Our research also investigates how to convert a set of reliable functional determinations into a minimal set of bifid dependencies, which can be used to represent the underlying data relationships in a more concise and meaningful way.

Dynamic models that account for time changes in time series data are crucial for accurately predicting future trends.  To address this, we developed a new statistical framework called the time-varying Poisson autoregressive model, which allows for the estimation of changing relationships between variables over time.  This model is based on a flexible approach to modeling time series data that incorporates the properties of the Gamma distribution and a novel method for estimating time-varying parameters.  We propose a novel estimation technique that combines a combination of a smoothing method and a Bayesian approach to obtain accurate parameter estimates.  Our approach is validated through a series of simulation studies and real-world data analysis, which demonstrate its effectiveness in recovering time-varying parameters and forecasting future values.  Our findings suggest that the time-varying Poisson autoregressive model can provide a more accurate and efficient way to model time series data that exhibit changing relationships between variables over time.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDF), a novel approach to representing objects that is invariant to their orientation in 3D space. Unlike previous methods, NDF is not limited to specific object poses and can be used for a range of object manipulation tasks, including contact-rich tasks. By integrating object pose with a point-wise property, NDF is able to achieve high performance in these tasks. In our experiments, NDF outperforms the current state-of-the-art in push task performance and shows promising results in more complex tasks.

This paper presents a revision of the SiD Sensor design, incorporating recent findings from the SiD collaboration and incorporating new CMS detector information. Key updates include a refined magnetic field value, enhanced pile-up data from the CMS, and a more accurate description of the SiD inner tracker's geometry.

We have conducted a detailed analysis of the stellar populations in the globular cluster Tonantzintla 2, which is located in the bulge of the Milky Way. By examining the spectra of 100 stars within the cluster, we have determined its chemical composition, specifically its levels of iron, alpha elements, and oxygen. Our findings indicate that the cluster has a metallicity of approximately 1.5 times that of the Sun, an alpha-enhancement of around 0.2 to 0.3 times that of the Sun, and a significant oxygen abundance spread of around 0.3 to 0.4 times that of the Sun. The oxygen levels within the cluster are also found to be lower than those typically observed in bulge clusters with similar metallicities. The age of the cluster is estimated to be around 10 to 12 billion years, and its stellar populations exhibit a range of characteristics, including variations in alpha and oxygen abundances, which are indicative of multiple stellar populations. The findings of our study provide valuable insights into the processes that have shaped the bulge of the Milky Way and the formation of stellar clusters within it.

This paper introduces a framework for analyzing and improving the Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs (Isabelle AFP), with a specific focus on theorem validation. We have employed this framework to assess the contents of the Isabelle AFP, resulting in the identification of 151 theorems that were either unproven or inadequately completed. To illustrate the effectiveness of our approach, we have contributed 11 proofs to the AFP, with 6 of these contributions being accepted into the archive.

We have determined the precise magnetic field at the Yang-Lee edge singularity for classical spin systems with symmetries of type O(N) in dimensions d greater than 2. Our findings, which are valid up to numerical uncertainties, have been calculated for various spin values of type 0 ≤ B and dimensions d equal to 3, 4, and effectively 5, using a combination of high-precision Monte Carlo simulations and epsilon expansion. Our results have been cross-verified and are in excellent agreement with previous studies.

We establish an enhanced version of the Sudakov-Fernique inequality specifically for the outputs of approximate message passing algorithms. This refinement enables us to derive an improved result concerning the local concavity of TAP free energy, and also provides a more concise proof of this finding. Additionally, our proof of the local concavity of TAP free energy is entirely self-contained.

This lecture will examine the use of full-wave electromagnetic simulations in analyzing and designing metasurfaces, which are ultra-thin electromagnetic structures composed of repeated unit cells. Full-wave simulations will be demonstrated as a means to accurately predict the behavior of metasurfaces in practical applications, such as in antenna design. A key aspect of this examination involves utilizing simulation tools to efficiently model the interaction between incident waves and the metasurface, allowing for the determination of key parameters such as reflection coefficients and transmission coefficients. These parameters can then be used to inform the design of antennas that incorporate metasurfaces, which can enhance their performance in a variety of ways. A key example of this involves the use of metasurfaces to create reflective surfaces that can be tuned to reflect electromagnetic waves in a variety of ways, such as in the design of phased array antennas. A key aspect of this involves the use of full-wave simulations to accurately predict the interaction between incident waves and the metasurface, allowing for the efficient design of antennas that incorporate these structures. A key example of this involves the use of metasurfaces to create reflective surfaces that can be tuned to reflect electromagnetic waves in a variety of ways, such as in the design of phased array antennas. A key aspect of this involves the use of full-wave simulations to accurately predict the interaction between incident waves and the metasurface, allowing for the efficient design of antennas that incorporate these structures.

The nonlinear orbital linearization problem asks whether a given vector field can be transformed into one whose orbits match those of a simpler, linear vector field through a nearby diffeomorphism. This transformation makes analyzing the original vector field's flow equivalent to analyzing the basic exponential flow of the transformed, linear vector field. Previous work has established sufficient conditions for smooth hyperbolic and fully integrable vector fields to have the property of orbital linearization.

The accuracy of chemical simulations relies heavily on the precision of electron correlation calculations, which can be achieved through the use of large basis sets and complete configuration interaction (CCI) expansions. However, the computational cost of CCI calculations becomes prohibitive for complex molecules. In this study, we introduce a novel deep learning approach that learns the CCI wavefunction of a molecular system, resulting in highly accurate predictions of total energies and electron density distributions. Our method is demonstrated on the water molecule, yielding near-chemical accuracy with a computational cost comparable to that of a single Hartree-Fock calculation.

We report an unusual massive star, designated HD 174938, which exhibits a significant gravitational redshift of 0.59 ± 0.05 km/s. This value is approximately three times the typical range for stars of its spectral type (A0). HD 174938 is a single star with a mass of 2.5 ± 0.1 M⊙, and it is surrounded by a circumstellar disk. The star's rotation is rapid, with a period of 0.51 days, and it is experiencing significant magnetic activity, as evidenced by the presence of starspots and X-ray emission. The star's light curve reveals a massive, elongated feature that spans 0.45 ± 0.05 of the star's surface, which may be a result of a close encounter with a passing companion.

This article provides an overview of using photometry from stars to study aerosols, 
highlighting key findings and discoveries made in this field over the past decade. 
It covers various types of planetary atmospheres, including terrestrial planets, 
super-Earths, and exo-Venus-like worlds, as well as the study of exoplanet host stars 
and the Sun. The article also discusses the challenges and limitations of this method, 
and how it can be used to study the evolution of planetary atmospheres.

This paper introduces a novel end-to-end pose estimation framework, DeepHMap++, which enhances our existing method, DeepHMap, by incorporating a projection grouping module. DeepHMap originally employed a correspondence learning module to identify keypoint correspondences, but this approach is limited to estimating six degrees of freedom pose from object points. To address this limitation, we developed the projection grouping module, which projects 3D object points onto a 2D image plane and clusters the resulting projections into multiple regions. Each of these regions is then assigned a region pose by a region pose estimation module. A correspondence learning module is employed to integrate the reliable six degrees of freedom pose from the object points and the unreliable region poses to produce a reliable pose estimate. We also introduce a correspondence cost function to optimize the correspondence learning module. Experimental results on the LINEMOD and ITU-PRR datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of DeepHMap++ in pose estimation.

Nonlocal continuum theories are gaining popularity in modeling materials with complex failure patterns, particularly those that can't be adequately described by classical mechanics. Bond-based peridynamics, a specific type of nonlocal continuum theory, has been widely used to simulate intricate fracture patterns in solids. This approach extends beyond peridynamics, however, and has been adapted for fluid dynamics simulations. This review explores the fundamentals of bond-based models, including peridynamics and its peridynamic equivalent, and discusses their applications in solid and fluid mechanics simulations.

A Graphical Lasso algorithm efficiently handles large-scale, sparse, and positively constrained covariance matrix computations. To address the increasing size of datasets, a Generalized Graphical Lasso (GGLasso) algorithm has been developed, which solves the problem for additional constraint matrices. This paper introduces GGLasso, a Python library that implements the GGLasso algorithm and provides a user-friendly interface for various applications, including precision medicine and financial risk management. The library is also available on PyPI for easy installation and use.

The challenges of predicting configurations for complex molecules are significant, particularly when dealing with large and interconnected systems.  To address this challenge, researchers have turned to molecular dynamics simulations, which have been particularly successful in predicting the structures of smaller molecules like proteins.  However, these methods have been less effective in predicting the structures of large molecular assemblies, such as DNA origami.  To overcome this challenge, researchers have developed a new method that combines stochastic dynamics with a robust optimization algorithm to efficiently sample the configurations of complex molecules.  This method has been tested on a variety of molecular systems, including proteins, DNA origami, and hybrid systems, and has been shown to be both accurate and computationally efficient.  The results of this study suggest that this method could be a valuable tool for predicting the structures of complex molecular systems.

We have simulated how binary black holes merge in an environment with wave dark energy, a type of low-energy matter. Our simulations show that binary black holes can emit wave dark energy, which can be a significant source of energy loss. This emission can be affected by the binary black hole's orbital motion and mass ratio, and it can also be influenced by gravitational waves. As a result, the merger time can be significantly reduced, and the final state of the black hole can be different from what is observed in a vacuum. These findings have important implications for understanding the behavior of binary black holes and the evolution of the universe.

This study investigates how the asymptotic behavior of a vibrating, flexible beam, modeled after Euler-Bernoulli principles, is influenced by its connection to a star graph. The graph consists of $N$ edges that converge at a single vertex, with no external forces acting on it. By applying a specific energy dissipation mechanism at the beam's free ends, we examine the stability properties of the system. Our analysis reveals that the system exhibits uniform $L^2$-decay at a rate of one, with distinct outcomes for odd and even values of $N$.

In photoacoustic tomography (PAT), a type of imaging that combines ultrasound and optical techniques, PAT systems that use an array of detectors covering a large area are becoming increasingly important.  However, a common issue with these detectors is the distortion of the acoustic waves as they pass through the material of the lens, which can affect the quality of the images produced.  In this study, a new substance called polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is introduced as a potential solution to this problem.  The material properties of PVDF are examined and compared to other common lens substances, and the effects of using PVDF lenses on the acoustic waves are simulated and tested.  The results show that using PVDF lenses can significantly reduce the distortion of the acoustic waves, and can even lead to an improvement in the quality of the images produced in PAT systems that use an array of detectors covering a large area.  These findings suggest that PVDF could be a promising new material for use in PAT systems.

The concept of node prominence has been extensively studied in single networks, yet its application to multilayer networks remains underdeveloped. This study introduces a novel approach to measuring node prominence in multilayer networks, which takes into account the interconnections between different network layers. This method is based on a newly devised metric, the eigenvector multilayer prominence (EMP), which is derived from the leading singular value of a specially constructed matrix. This matrix is formed by combining the adjacency matrices of the individual network layers, weighted according to their respective importance. The EMP is shown to be mathematically equivalent to the leading singular value of this matrix, and its underlying mechanism is explained through the lens of singular value decomposition. The study also presents an alternative calculation method for the EMP, which is based on a specially defined multilayer matrix. The proposed approach is validated through a case study involving the identification of influential nodes in the stock market, and the results demonstrate that the EMP outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy. The study also highlights the potential for the EMP to be used for node recommendation and network compression, and the findings are supported by additional analyses. The study also discusses the limitations of the proposed approach, and the results demonstrate that the EMP can be effectively used for a range of multilayer network applications. The study also presents the source code for the proposed method, which is available for download. The findings of this study contribute to the broader understanding of multilayer network analysis,

We introduce a novel approach to image restoration that combines multiple
degradation removal tasks, such as deblurring, demosaicking, and denoising,
into a collaborative framework. This collaborative method leverages the
inherent connection between these tasks and utilizes a mosaic blur kernel to
capture the combined effect of all degradations on raw images. By training a
single network on this combined data, we achieve a more efficient and
effective solution that outperforms a sequential approach of performing each
task individually. Our experiments on public datasets demonstrate the
effectiveness of our collaborative method, which yields significant
improvements in terms of both PSNR and visual quality compared to the
sequential baseline.

We derive the form of Dirac's equation under the conditions of $R$-Minkowski spacetime, 
and demonstrate that it can be obtained from the Schr\"odinger equation modified by 
Bargmann's theorem, which accounts for the noncommutative nature of spacetime.

This paper introduces a Python package, the Causal Exploration Toolbox, which
facilitates the use of various causal inference methods. The toolbox is designed
to be flexible, allowing users to easily incorporate additional algorithms and
models. The package includes built-in tools for exploring and visualizing causal
connections, which can be applied to both observational and experimental data
sets. The Causal Exploration Toolbox is particularly useful for researchers and
practitioners who are interested in gaining a deeper understanding of the causal
mechanisms underlying complex data sets.

This study investigates how solid objects interact with liquid surfaces, specifically examining the process of spheres entering a liquid surface from a state of free fall. We focus on a moderate speed range and develop a theoretical model to describe the forces involved, taking into account surface tension, viscous forces, and the sphere's speed of entry. We also validate our model through a combination of theoretical analysis and numerical simulations, which reveal that the seal time is determined by the balance between the sphere's kinetic energy and the liquid's surface tension. We also explore the effects of the sphere's size and the liquid's viscosity on the seal time, which has implications for the design of microfluidic devices and other applications.

We investigate the implications of nonperturbative effects in Type IIB compactifications, specifically those involving M5-branes and instantons, on global symmetries and possible extensions of the superpotential. Our analysis reveals that M5-branes and instantons break a U(1) R-symmetry globally, and we find that certain combinations of effects can be described as extended theta-terms. We then examine the implications of these findings on the axio-dilaton sector and discuss how they relate to the generation of small positive cosmological constants in string theory.

Confidential computing is a security measure that protects sensitive data from being compromised, even when the computing hardware is untrusted.  This type of security is commonly achieved through physically isolated hardware, which relies on hardware-based encryption to ensure data remains secure.  However, this approach has a significant flaw: it is vulnerable to side-channel attacks, which can be used to extract sensitive information from the data.  As a result, researchers have been forced to develop complex and costly solutions to mitigate these attacks.  In this paper, we take a different approach by focusing on minimizing an attacker's confidence in any information they may have gained from side-channel attacks, even when the hardware is used for only a single purpose.  We introduce a novel, lightweight hardware solution called Minimizing Confidence with Solely-Used Hardware (MCHWH), which is designed to minimize the amount of information that can be extracted from side-channel attacks.  MCHWH is based on a novel design that uses a combination of randomization and masking to obscure sensitive information from attackers.  Our results show that MCHWH is highly effective at minimizing confidence, reducing the amount of information that can be extracted from side-channel attacks by up to 99.99999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999

Reinforcement learning in a distributed setup is commonly used in practice, 
where the learning agent is frequently subjected to communication failures 
with the central server. 
These problems can lead to significant corruption of gradient information, 
which can severely hinder the performance of reinforcement learning algorithms. 
In this paper, we examine the impact of highly corrupted gradient information 
on policy optimization in a reinforcement learning context and develop a new 
resilient policy gradient algorithm to counteract this issue. 
Our proposed method is capable of withstanding severe information corruption 
and successfully recovers the optimal policy even in the presence of such 
adversarial interference. 
We also demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm through experiments 
on a standard reinforcement learning benchmark, showing its superiority over 
existing resilient methods.

In the conundrum of the selectionless box game, players are required to guess the contents of a box, which can either hold a quarter or a ping pong ball, based solely on the sound it makes when shaken. Notably, this task becomes significantly more challenging when the quarter is present, as it produces a sound that is indistinguishable from that of the ping pong ball. To address this issue, we have devised a novel approach, which involves using a microphone to record the sound and a machine learning algorithm to analyze the resulting data. Our research reveals that this approach can be solved with remarkable accuracy, exceeding 90%, using a simple algorithm known as a perceptron. Furthermore, our results suggest that the human brain may employ a more sophisticated mechanism, which involves a form of Bayesian inference, to solve this conundrum.

We have conducted a comprehensive study of the electronic and magnetic properties of cupricite, a mineral with the cupric structure, using high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy and advanced theoretical calculations. Our findings reveal that cupricite exhibits distinct orbital-selective behavior, where the electronic and magnetic characteristics of copper and iron are significantly different due to their distinct d-orbitals. Specifically, we found that the copper d-x2-y2 orbital is responsible for its localized magnetic moment, while the more complex, multi-orbital system of iron leads to its local electronic and charge fluctuations. Our results provide a clear example of orbital-selective behavior in a natural mineral and suggest that cupricite could be used as a valuable model system for studying this phenomenon.

We have successfully demonstrated rapid Rabi oscillations in excitons within GaAs quantum wells, exhibiting a frequency 10 times higher than previously reported, using linearly polarized light and short laser pulses. This breakthrough was achieved without the need for external magnetic fields or circularly polarized light, and our findings are corroborated by accurate simulations.

In two-dimensional non-symmorphic wallpaper lattice structures, Dirac points are found at high symmetry points in the Brillouin zone, which can be adjusted through interlayer interactions. In this study, we examine a non-symmorphic wallpaper lattice lattice with a triangular basis and discover that, without interlayer interactions, it contains two distinct types of Dirac points: one at the K point and another at the R point. By introducing interlayer interactions, we find that the interplay between these two types of Dirac points can be used to control their positions in the Brillouin zone, potentially leading to the creation of flat bands.

Quantum-optical catalysis is an advanced technique that enables the generation of unique quantum states, such as Fock states and coherent states, by transforming weak input light into highly non-classical states of light. This breakthrough method has been successfully applied to create quantum states with up to 10 photons, but scaling this achievement to higher photon numbers has proven challenging. In this research, we demonstrate a novel approach to generating single-photon facilitated coherent states, or FCSs, using quantum-optical catalysis. These FCSs, which exhibit a superposition of zero and one-photon number states, are highly non-classical and can be used to enhance various quantum sensing and metrology applications. By developing a new detection scheme, we successfully measured the FCS and obtained up to 9.5 dB of squeezing, a significant achievement that paves the way for further exploration of quantum-optical catalysis in the realm of continuous-variable quantum information processing.

In the context of the Newman-Penrose formalism for general relativity, we provide a comprehensive explanation of the geometric and physical significance behind the six complex components of a bivector expressed in a null tetrad basis. This explanation is applicable to both vacuum and non-vacuum spacetimes. We initially examine the null and non-null characteristics of such bivectors, specifically focusing on their relationships to congruences of null and timelike geodesics. Subsequently, we explore how the NP framework can be utilized to analyze the properties of the Weyl and Einstein tensors in spacetimes containing matter fields, thereby revealing how the six components of a bivector can be represented through the complex scalar components of the Weyl curvature tensor in the NP formalism. As an illustrative example, we investigate the Kretschmann scalar of the Reissner-Nordström spacetime, demonstrating how its value can be derived from the six complex components of a charged bivector.

Identifying the correct polymer formula from a compound's elemental composition is a key step in determining its structure.  Given the vast number of possible combinations of atoms, a reliable method is needed to derive the polymer's chemical formula.  A new approach is proposed that uses linear regression to establish a relationship between a compound's molecular weight and its atom counts, followed by integer optimization to find the formula that best matches the data.  This method is demonstrated to be effective in deriving the chemical formulas of both organic and inorganic compounds, including proteins.

This paper introduces a straightforward method for modeling dynamic systems by directly transcribing their governing equations into a simulation framework. We demonstrate how this method can be employed to simulate dual-patient interactions during the COVID-19 pandemic, specifically focusing on the effects of breathing vibrations on viral transmission. By utilizing a state-space optimization approach, we achieve a high level of accuracy in our simulation, with a maximum absolute error of 0.0001 compared to a benchmark solution. We also provide a step-by-step guide for readers to replicate our results.

Identifying and segmenting tumors in the esophagus from CT images is a crucial task in medical image analysis, which aids doctors in making accurate diagnoses and treatment plans. However, this task is challenging due to the low contrast between the esophagus and tumors, as well as the varying shapes and sizes of the esophagus. In this study, a novel deep learning model called DDAUnet is proposed to address these challenges. DDAUnet is an improved version of the Unet architecture, which incorporates two key innovations: dilated convolution and attention gates. The experimental results show that DDAUnet outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in terms of Dice Similarity Coefficient, Hausdorff Distance, and Average Symmetric Surface Distance metrics.

This paper introduces a collective learning approach to analyzing well logs, which involves training a neural network to replicate the behavior of a human expert who interprets well logs and makes decisions during geosteering. By leveraging the capabilities of supervised learning, we can quantify the uncertainty associated with the predictions made by the neural network, which is achieved through Bayesian neural networks. We demonstrate this approach using a case study of a well being drilled in the North Sea, where the goal is to maintain the well within a specific target zone. We compare the predictions made by the collective-based neural network to those of a traditional well log interpretation method, which involves using a gamma ray and resistivity tool to determine the well's position. We find that the Bayesian neural network's predictions are in good agreement with the traditional method, and that the uncertainty associated with the predictions is consistent with the expected level of uncertainty. We also discuss the potential benefits of using this approach, which includes the ability to identify areas where the neural network's predictions are less certain, and to use this information to make more informed decisions during geosteering.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing, and existing methods typically tackle it by identifying entity boundaries and assigning labels to individual entities. In contrast, our approach views NER as a task of parsing the holistic sentence structure, and proposes Nested Sentence Structure Parsing (NSSP), a new framework that captures the nested entity relationships and sentence structure simultaneously. Our NSSP model employs a customized nested stack LSTMs architecture to model the complex entity hierarchy and sentence structure, and achieves superior performance on two widely used NER benchmarks, including the MSRA and CoNLL-2003 datasets.

We develop a method to count and analyze the geometric properties of real and rational bitangent planes to a specific type of quartic surfaces in three-dimensional space, using tropical geometry. This approach involves constructing a tropicalization of a family of surfaces, which allows us to study the corresponding surfaces in three-dimensional space. By applying this method, we are able to count and analyze the real and rational bitangents to the original surface, as well as verify a conjecture made by Allcock regarding the rationality of certain 27 lines on a specific type of quartic surface.

This paper introduces a novel approach to locating sensors in wireless sensor networks, which accounts for cross-technology interference. We employ three anchor nodes and numerous sensor nodes within the network, and we analyze the network's performance in relation to interference caused by different communication technologies. We develop a new algorithm that leverages an interference-aware distance measurement model to enhance the accuracy of node positioning. We also investigate the impact of various factors, including network size, node distribution, and interference levels, on the overall performance of the algorithm. Our results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods by significantly reducing the average error in node positioning.

Multilingual individuals who switch between two languages while communicating often blend them together, resulting in a code-mixed language. This phenomenon is widespread and occurs in various multilingual communities, making it a significant area of study in natural language processing. Researchers have extensively studied code-mixed languages, yet there are still unresolved issues that require further investigation. This paper delves into the intricacies of code-mixed NLP, highlighting the challenges and underlying factors that influence multilingual NLP tasks. By examining the underlying factors, we aim to provide a comprehensive understanding of code-mixed NLP and offer potential avenues for future research.

Evaluating the quality of descriptions generated by machines is a significant challenge in Natural Language Generation. Human references are commonly used for comparison, but they are costly to obtain and require a significant amount of time. To address this issue, we propose a new method for assessing machine-generated descriptions that relies on human information, which can be collected more efficiently through a web-based interface. This approach allows for the collection of human data on a large scale, resulting in a more comprehensive and diverse dataset. We conducted a series of experiments to test the effectiveness of our method, which showed that it produces comparable results to human references, but with a significant reduction in time and cost.

The crystal structure of Ta$_2$O$_5$ in its metastable $\delta$-phase has been extensively studied, with a focus on its complex phase diagram and various applications. A key aspect of this research is the $\delta$-phase's potential to transform into the $\gamma$-phase, which has a more stable crystal structure. To better understand this transition, researchers have employed density functional theory and Monte Carlo simulations to analyze the Ta$_2$O$_5$ crystal structure. By systematically varying lattice parameters and exploring the potential energy landscape, a new, lower energy crystal structure has been identified, which closely resembles the $\gamma$-phase. This new structure is predicted to be the ground state of Ta$_2$O$_5$, with a significantly lower energy than the previously known $\delta$-phase.

This study investigates the spread of misinformation on Reddit, a popular online platform, by analyzing the role of the Big Geographic Sort (BGS) feature. The BGS feature, which organizes content by geographic location, has been found to increase the spread of misinformation among Reddit users. By analyzing the behavior of users on the r/AskReddit subreddit, researchers discovered that the BGS feature leads to a decrease in the likelihood of a post being flagged as false, but this effect is more pronounced among users who are less likely to engage in online discussions. The study also found that the BGS feature leads to a decrease in the diversity of opinions expressed in comments, but this effect is more pronounced among users who are less likely to agree with other users. The study suggests that the BGS feature may contribute to the spread of misinformation and the polarization of opinions, and calls for further research into the role of online platform design in shaping user behavior.

The speed at which information spreads through social networks has increased
dramatically in recent times, fueled by the widespread adoption of the internet.
This rapid dissemination of information can unfortunately facilitate the spread
of misinformation and manipulation, which can have serious consequences.
Although various methods have been developed to detect misinformation and
manipulation, they often rely on assumptions that are difficult to meet in
practice, such as the availability of ground truth labels. In this study, we
propose a new approach to identifying suspicious occurrences in real-time
information flows, which we call SUSP. Our method is designed to be label-free,
interpretable, and capable of operating in real-time. We demonstrate the
effectiveness of our approach through experiments on real-world datasets,
including the 2016 US Presidential Election Twitter stream and the 2019
European Parliament elections Twitter stream. Our results show that our method
can accurately identify periods of high misinformation and manipulation, as
well as periods of coordinated inauthentic behavior.

This study aims to investigate the underlying principles of how human teachers verbally instruct robots during manipulation tasks. To do this, we gathered a dataset consisting of 100 training and 50 validation examples, where human instructors demonstrated and provided spoken guidance on various object use tasks to a robot. The data was used to train a spoken instruction model, which outperformed a baseline that relied on written instructions. Notably, the human-provided verbal cues were found to be more concise than expected, often consisting of just a few words, and this approach significantly improved the robot's ability to complete tasks.

A tree structure consists of nodes that can have varying numbers of child nodes, known as degree. We've developed a technique to generate trees randomly with different degrees, called the sampling method. This technique relies on a previously established approach by Aldous and applies to all possible sequences of node degree combinations. We've also identified conditions for the method's applicability and demonstrated its effectiveness through multiple examples, including all possible node degree combinations.

Conformal field theory (CFT) intricacy can be analyzed through a mathematical framework, specifically the isomonodromic deformation of linear differential equations. This study reveals a deeper understanding of the relationship between CFT and monodromy data by exploring the Ising model within this framework. It derives differential equations for CFT correlation functions and derives explicit solutions for three-point functions and conformal blocks. These findings demonstrate that the connection between CFT and monodromy data can be described using Grassmannian manifolds, providing a geometric perspective on the field.

Conversational agents are increasingly being used in customer service, but their
effectiveness is hindered by the lack of reliable testing methods.
Current approaches to testing these systems are either too costly, require human
input, or are limited to specific applications.
We propose a new testing framework that employs generative adversarial networks
to create a large dataset of realistic human conversations, which can be used to
automatically assess the performance of conversational agents.
Our approach generates a large dataset of synthetic dialogues, which is then used
to train a model that predicts the quality of the tested system's responses.
Our framework is capable of producing a large dataset of realistic human conversations,
which is then used to evaluate the performance of the tested system.
Our approach is also capable of generating a large dataset of realistic human conversations,
which is then used to evaluate the performance of the tested system.

A hypothetical Planet X, with a semi-major axis exceeding 200 AU, has been proposed to explain the unusual orbital characteristics of the Kuiper Belt. This planet's gravitational influence on the orbits of the Solar System's major bodies is so minimal that it is undetectable with the current level of precision in ephemerides. However, a more massive Planet X, with a mass greater than 5 Earth masses, would have a noticeable effect on the orbits of the known planets, which can be detected with the precision achieved by the JPL DE440 ephemeris. This effect would be most evident in the form of a secular acceleration in the planets' orbital periods, which can be measured by comparing the observed periods with the periods predicted by the DE440 ephemeris. The magnitude of this acceleration is directly proportional to the semi-major axis of Planet X's orbit, which can be used to estimate the planet's mass and location. The constraints on the mass and location of Planet X are most stringent for orbits with a semi-major axis between 200 and 400 AU, which is consistent with the preferred range of semi-major axes for the hypothetical Planet X.

The growing amount of scientific data and the rapid pace of discoveries have made it difficult for researchers to keep up with the latest breakthroughs in their field. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach to automatically generating research summaries that combine multiple sources of information. Our method leverages a machine reading comprehension model and a translation-agnostic multi-lingual architecture to create concise explanations of a specific topic based on a single research paper and a pool of related articles in the same language. We further enhance our approach by incorporating a monolingual translation archive, which allows us to utilize high-quality translations between different languages. Our method has been tested on the T2A and the Cross-Topic evaluation datasets, and the results show that it outperforms the state-of-the-art monolingual baseline by a significant margin.

Conformal Cyclic Cosmology (CCC) proposes that the future universe's ultimate heat death will resemble the Big Bang's initial conditions, thus making the beginning and end of the universe fundamentally similar. To test this hypothesis, researchers have sought to identify specific patterns in the cosmic microwave background that could indicate the presence of primordial gravitational waves or other anomalies. One such pattern involves the alignment of temperature fluctuations in adjacent regions of the sky, which would be a signature of the CCC theory. Another proposed signature is the existence of low-variance regions in the CMB sky, which would be indicative of the initial conditions of the universe. In this paper, we examine the validity of these two tests by analyzing the statistical properties of the CMB sky and comparing them to the predictions of the standard cosmological model. Our results show that the observed temperature fluctuations and low-variance regions are consistent with the predictions of the standard model and do not provide strong evidence for the CCC theory.

This paper demonstrates that the fractional Yamabe evolution equation has convergent solutions under specific conditions. An auxiliary parabolic equation is introduced to establish this convergence, and the main result is derived from the auxiliary equation's properties.

Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success in various tasks, but their effectiveness relies heavily on large annotated datasets. In contrast, humans can learn new concepts from limited examples by using prototypes that represent typical examples of a concept. This research proposes a new approach to few-sample learning that combines prototype learning with generative models. The approach involves training a neural network to generate typical samples for each class based on limited annotated data, which can then be used to accurately classify new, unlabeled data. The network is trained using a combination of classification and generative losses, which are optimized through an alternating training process. The results show that this approach outperforms existing methods on multiple benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, and can learn from as few as 5 samples per class.

A novel recommendation approach, called Multi-Sparse-Domain Cooperative Recommendation (MSDCR), is introduced to tackle the issue of limited data availability in individual domains. By integrating multiple domains, MSDCR leverages a more comprehensive set of user-item interactions to enhance preference learning. To achieve this, it employs a multi-task learning framework that combines three types of preference representations: explicit preferences from each domain, implicit preferences from each domain, and a more holistic preference from the combined dataset. To facilitate effective knowledge transfer across domains, a cross-domain preference propagation module is incorporated into the framework. Experimental results demonstrate that MSDCR outperforms existing recommendation methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.

This paper introduces a novel approach to optimizing conic expressions,
focusing on the efficient handling of the natural cone in second-order cone
programming. A key contribution is the development of Hypatia.jl, a specialized
optimization package that leverages the native capabilities of the JuMP and
HiGHS solvers. By utilizing the natural cone, Hypatia.jl eliminates the need
for variable transformations, which can introduce numerical inaccuracies.
Numerical experiments demonstrate that utilizing the natural cone with Hypatia.jl
can lead to more accurate and reliable optimization results.

This study investigates the challenges of training deep learning models for MRI quality assurance, specifically focusing on the difficulties of model generalization. Our research reveals that the poor performance of these models on unseen data is a common issue, which we attribute to overfitting and the generation of spurious correlations. To address this problem, we employ a hypothesis-driven approach to identify the underlying causes of the models' failures. Our experiments demonstrate that the models are prone to overfitting and are influenced by irrelevant MRI artifacts. To mitigate this issue, we employ a novel data augmentation technique that simulates various imaging artifacts, thereby improving the models' ability to generalize. Our results show that this approach significantly enhances the performance of the models on unseen data, achieving a substantial improvement in accuracy. Our research also highlights the importance of rigorous testing and evaluation of deep learning models for MRI quality assurance, emphasizing the need for a more robust and reliable assessment methodology.

With the rise in private vehicle ownership, there's a growing concern about their environmental impact. As a result, many countries are promoting private electric vehicles (EVs) to reduce pollution and conserve non-renewable energy. However, the widespread adoption of EVs poses a potential threat to power distribution networks, which supply the necessary charging infrastructure. This paper introduces a novel approach to enhance the resilience of distribution networks by considering the impact of private EVs. The proposed method employs a multi-agent optimization framework to balance the charging needs of EVs with the stability of the power grid. This approach allows for the efficient allocation of charging resources while maintaining network reliability. The results of the study demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the resilience of distribution networks.

Intel's Optane DC Persistent Storage Module, a new type of memory, is designed to be used as an extension of a computer's main memory while retaining data even when the system is shut down. This innovative technology is expected to significantly enhance the performance of data-intensive applications, particularly those that require frequent updates and updates to a large dataset. In this study, we evaluate the performance of Optane DC Persistent Memory in various scenarios, including a custom benchmark and real-world applications, such as a database management system and a data analytics tool. Our findings show that Optane DC Persistent Memory outperforms traditional DRAM in terms of speed and data retention, but also reveals some limitations, such as slower write speeds and potential data corruption issues. Our results provide valuable insights into the potential capabilities and constraints of this new type of memory, and can guide future research and development in the field.

In large-scale traffic management, the meeting problem is a crucial sub-task that involves multiple autonomous vehicles coordinating to reach a common location at the same time. This paper introduces a novel incentive-based approach, the Multi-Agent Recurrent Meeting (MARM) algorithm, which enables traffic participants to reach a common point in time and space. MARM utilizes a recurrent neural network to learn a policy that minimizes the discrepancy between a vehicle's actual trajectory and an ideal trajectory, which is determined by a meeting incentive function. This function is based on a time-space graph and is optimized to maximize the probability of all vehicles meeting at a common point. We demonstrate the effectiveness of MARM through simulations, showing that it outperforms existing methods in terms of both efficiency and safety.

This study explores the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm(1-x)Sn3 (x=0.25, 0.5, 0.75) using first-principles calculations within the local density approximation and the spin-polarized DFT+U method. Our findings indicate that all compounds adopt the AuCu3-type structure, with lattice parameters and bulk moduli aligning with experimental data. GdSn3 and CmSn3 exhibit p-d hybridization, with CmSn3 showing a higher degree of hybridization. Both GdSn3 and CmSn3 display ferromagnetic ordering, with GdSn3 having a higher magnetic moment. The study also reveals that the GdxCm(1-x)Sn3 series exhibits a transition from ferromagnetic to antiferromagnetic behavior at x=0.75.

The Standard Model of particle physics has been extensively validated, yet there are still unexplained aspects, particularly concerning dark matter and the universe's matter-antimatter imbalance. This paper presents a theoretical framework that attributes dark matter to extra quarks and mesons, as well as the universe's baryon asymmetry to additional generations of quarks. The model's constraints are analyzed, and the expected properties of the extra quarks and mesons are predicted.
This paper provides a novel proof of the basis for B-type Coxeter group generators, utilizing the concept of simple reflection as the starting point.

We investigated the possibility of using gravitational lensing to enhance the brightness of distant supernovae, and identified a method to estimate the lensing effect based on the apparent size of the host galaxies of these supernovae. By applying this method to the Pantheon sample of 1038 Type Ia supernovae, we found that a significant number of them appear to be lensed, and that the lensing effect is consistent with theoretical predictions. We also found that the lensing effect is too small to be detected in the Pantheon sample, and that our method can be used to identify a small number of supernovae that are significantly lensed. We also found that the lensing effect is consistent with the predictions of the standard cosmological model, and that our method can be used to constrain the parameters of this model. We also found that the lensing effect is consistent with the predictions of the standard model of particle physics, and that our method can be used to search for new physics beyond this model.

This introduction outlines the fundamental concepts of stochastic partial differential equations, which arise from the interplay between the randomness inherent in stochastic processes and the deterministic nature of partial differential equations.

This research introduces a novel design for silicon-on-insulator (SOI) material that incorporates T-shaped waveguide structures, which significantly enhance third-order nonlinear optical effects. By utilizing a two-wavelength four-channel T-hub setup, researchers can achieve efficient all-optical signal switching with a control pulse energy as low as 0.15 pJ at 1550 nm. This process involves the generation of a 1525 nm photon through four-photon absorption and subsequent energy transfer to other channels, resulting in the emission of a 1550 nm photon.

MRI technology has significantly improved medical diagnosis, enabling doctors to
visually assess internal organs and body parts. MRI images are generated by
detecting radio waves emitted from hydrogen atoms within the body, providing a
clear and detailed view of the anatomy. These images are crucial for identifying
abnormalities, including tumors, which can be detected through various methods,
such as CT scans, X-rays, and biopsies. However, early diagnosis is essential for
effective treatment, and computer-aided detection systems can play a vital role in
aiding doctors by analyzing MRI images and identifying potential tumors. This paper
reviews different image analysis methods used for tumor detection in MRI images,
including image segmentation techniques such as thresholding, region growing,
and active contours, as well as machine learning approaches like SVM and CNN. The
research presented in this paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of
current techniques and highlight the need for further investigation into more
advanced methods for accurate and reliable tumor detection in MRI images.

This paper introduces a novel algebraic approach to determining Bernoulli number ratios using polynomial matrices, building on previous work by various researchers. We define a specific ring of diagonalizable matrices and construct a polynomial matrix within this ring whose Bernoulli number ratios can be calculated through exact linear algebra methods.

The study investigates the impact of line catalogs on stellar activity noise in least-squares deconvolution (LSD) line-profiles, which is a critical factor in the LSS technique's performance. Researchers analyzed the relationship between the size and composition of line catalogs and the resulting activity noise in LSS profiles. By examining various line catalogs, they found that the size of the catalog has a more significant effect on activity noise than its composition. The study also explored the influence of line selection on activity noise, particularly in the context of LSD. The results indicate that the line selection can be randomized without affecting the activity noise, as long as the catalog size is maintained. The study provides a framework for understanding the relationship between line catalogs and activity noise in LSS profiles, which can inform future research in this area.

A critical issue in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) is the energy drain caused by frequent data collection and dissemination, which can be mitigated through a technique called on-demand gathering. This technique allows the base station to activate a specific area of the WSN, enabling it to collect data and disseminate it to the base station. To minimize energy consumption, a method is proposed that involves dividing the WSN into hierarchical scope sectors, with each sector having a different level of connectivity. By activating only a specific sector, the base station can collect data and disseminate it to the WSN with minimal energy consumption. A bidirectional link caliber estimation method is also proposed to estimate the distance between the base station and the activated sector, which is used to estimate the energy consumption of the WSN. The proposed method is shown to be effective in reducing energy consumption while maintaining high data collection and dissemination rates.

This paper introduces a novel dataset, CO-DETRAC, which consists of 10 distinct driving scenarios, totaling 20 contexts, each featuring a unique set of environmental conditions. To evaluate the performance of deep object detectors in various contexts, we conducted experiments using the DETRAC dataset, which was trained on a single context and tested across all driving scenarios in the CO-DETRAC. The results indicate that deep object detectors' performance is significantly influenced by context, with a 20% drop in mean Average Precision (mAP) observed when the detector is tested in an unfamiliar context. Furthermore, we found that object detectors' performance is highly correlated with the similarity between training and testing contexts, with a 0.8 correlation coefficient observed.

The research paper focuses on a system of elliptic equations, where the equations are not uniformly related to Kirchhoff type and include singular terms with exponential growth, specifically a Trudinger-Moser type. The study employs a variational approach to establish the existence of a solution to this system.

This paper presents concise, previously unpublished, concentration inequalities for independent and identically distributed binary random variables that exhibit certain types of negative dependence, including negative circular and negative association.

Let $K$ be a complete discrete valuation field with mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, whose residue field is finitely generated over $\mathbb{F}_p$. Let $R$ be the ring of integers of $K$, and $A_{\text{inf}}$ be the relative Fontaine ring over $R$. This paper establishes a relative de Rham comparison theorem, showing that the natural map from $A_{\text{inf}}$-modules to de Rham modules is an equivalence, with $A_{\text{inf}}$ being a finite $R$-algebra and de Rham modules being finite $R$-modules.

The proposed sideward deviation angle of the dihadron production cross-section, relative to the spin axis, holds significant potential for enhancing spin asymmetry measurements in Semi-Inclusive Deep Inelastic Scattering (SIDIS). This paper delves into the origin of this deviation by analyzing the contributions from the cos(phi_R) Fourier component of the dihadron production rate, specifically focusing on the interactions between a struck quark and two independent sea quarks. Our calculations, based on the twist-3 collinear mechanism, incorporate quark-antiquark correlations described by the twist-2 Boer-Mulders and twist-3 quark-sea quark correlator functions. By comparing our findings with previous research, we discover that the dihadron rate is primarily driven by the interference between the quark helicity and the quark-sea quark correlation, resulting in a substantial interference effect that surpasses the contribution from the Boer-Mulders function.

We examine the implications of Fock's 1932 discovery that the Schrödinger equation for a particle in a linear potential can be solved using de Sitter space geometry. This discovery is revisited in the context of de Sitter quantum field theory, where we find that the time evolution of a harmonic oscillator in de Sitter space is equivalent to the Fock effect, with the de Sitter factor $e^{\pi\lambda}$ emerging as a direct consequence. This connection is further explored by considering a de Sitter harmonic oscillator in interaction with a linearly accelerating particle, where the de Sitter factor is shown to be directly related to the particle's acceleration. This relationship is then applied to a cosmological model, where the de Sitter factor is shown to be directly related to the Hubble constant.

This note explores the notion of symplectic alterations, which are symplectic maps that transform a given smooth manifold into another, maintaining the overall structure. We establish the continuity of these alterations under the $C^\infty$-topology, mirroring a recent finding regarding contact alterations. The continuous nature of symplectic alterations enables the extension of various topological and differential properties from the altered manifold to the original one. As an illustration, we can continuously deform the symplectic capacity of a ball under gradual changes.

The entity suggestion task involves predicting the user's intended entity from their input, which can be represented as a sequence of characters or words. This paper proposes a novel approach to entity suggestion by utilizing the hierarchical structure of a Wikipedia graph. Our method leverages the graph's layered representation to capture both the local context of a node and the global connectivity of the graph. We employ a combination of a DeepWalk algorithm and a character-level Long Short-Term Memory network to convert the graph representation into a character-level sequence. Experimental results on the English Wikipedia dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in entity suggestion, achieving a mean average precision of 0.800.

The concept of ideal acceptance for incompatible kidney transplants is introduced, which is the minimum cost at which a transplant can be successfully performed. A mathematical model is developed to model the success of transplants, considering the cost of the procedure, the cost of living with a failing kidney, and the cost of a failed kidney. The model is then used to analyze the ideal acceptance cost for compatible and incompatible kidney transplants, considering the cost of bidding for organs. The results show that ideal acceptance for compatible transplants is determined solely by the cost of the procedure, whereas ideal acceptance for incompatible transplants is influenced by the cost of living with a failing kidney and the cost of a failed kidney. The model is then applied to a numerical example, which shows that the cost of living with a failing kidney is a significant factor in determining ideal acceptance for incompatible transplants. The model is then used to explore the implications of the model on the allocation of organs, which shows that the model can be used to improve the efficiency of organ allocation. The model is then used to explore the limitations of the model, which shows that the model can be used to improve the efficiency of organ allocation, but it is limited by the assumption that the cost of the procedure is the only factor in determining ideal acceptance.
